name: Therapeutic tai chi (Tai Ji Quan: Moving for Better Balance) course for high-fall-risk older adults
appliesWhen: The marginal gift funds additional places in a fidelity-specified 24-week, twice-weekly TJQMBB course for older adults at high fall risk.
doesNotApplyWhen: The course is shorter general tai chi (e.g. six-week Sun-style) or recruits relatively well older adults; Day et al. 2015 found no benefit there.
The program is a falls-risk home-modification or medication-review service.

nativeOutcome.unit: additional fidelity-equivalent high-risk participants completing a 24-week course
nativeOutcome.notes: Falls averted would be the better native unit (Li et al. 2018 reports fall incidence vs stretching). v1 keeps the SF utility pathway, so native outcome is a quality-weighted output, not a health outcome.

qalyBridge.notes: Linear onset to an endpoint utility gain over a six-month horizon, with no persistence. The endpoint coefficient is ambiguous in the source (see origin).

default.rationale: 24 weeks x 2 classes, per the trial protocol.

sources.title: Therapeutic tai ji quan randomized trial

paidHoursPerClass.label: Paid instructor preparation and delivery hours per class

default.rationale: SF planning assumption: one hour delivery plus one hour preparation/travel.

instructorHourlyCost.label: Loaded instructor cost per paid hour

preferredSources: BLS OEWS metro-area wage for Fitness Trainers and Instructors (39-9031), times a benefits/overhead load
lookup.fallback: None; this is the main local cost lookup.
lookup.judgmentGuide: SF used $60/hour, an assumed wage, not a quote.

supportCostPerParticipant.label: Licensing, room, outreach and screening cost per participant

lookup.fallback: SF $200 scaled by local/SF cost ratio, flagged as transferred judgment.

localTransfer.label: Local fidelity and population retention of the trial effect

preferredSources: Whether instructors are certified TJQMBB trainers
Availability of comparable free classes (the trial control was stretching, not nothing)

additionality.label: Share of funded places that are net-new capacity

preferredSources: Older Americans Act Title III-D evidence-based program funding through the local Area Agency on Aging

hypothesizedEndpointUtility.label: Hypothesized endpoint utility gain versus stretching

default.rationale: Independent calibration of .04. The source table labels .04 as incremental QALYs while its prose describes a utility difference; reading it as integrated QALYs would lower the price 4x. Unit ambiguity is unresolved.
Rounded six-month horizon; no persistence beyond follow-up.

onsetFraction.label: Average fraction of endpoint benefit realized over follow-up

default.rationale: 0.5 assumes linear growth from zero to endpoint.

excludedEffects: Fall injuries, mortality and healthcare savings on top of utility
Six-week Sun-style courses treated as the 24-week trial
nullBoundary: Null or harm remains possible. Zero additionality or a non-fidelity course gives no finite price.

origin.reproduces: The SF $600 course cost is the rounded output of the derived courseCost formula ($584 at $60/hour, 15 participants, $200 support). With courseCost fixed at $600 and all other p50 inputs, reproduces the SF central $2,400,000 per 10 QALYs; the unrounded formula gives $2,336,000. Change: the SF scenarios varied courseCost $300 to $1,200 as one judgment, which the template splits into wage, class size and support lookups.
